findings.title: New abstract order() breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java line 44 the interface adds abstract method int order(). Any third-party CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError/NoSuchMethodError and will fail to compile against the new interface. This is a binary and source incompatible change. It should be a default method e.g. default int order() { return 0; } to preserve compatibility.

findings.title: Same order for all server providers makes selection nondeterministic
findings.body: In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java line 57 detectProvider sorts by order reversed and picks element 0. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns 100. For equal order ServiceLoader order is classpath dependent, so a classpath containing both FIPS and non-FIPS/default providers now silently picks an arbitrary one instead of failing fast as before. Previously multiple providers threw IllegalStateException. Silently picking non-FIPS when FIPS is required (or vice versa) is a compliance and security failure and masks misconfiguration.

findings.title: readSequence does not enforce exact length match
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java line 57 readSequence loops while(length>0) subtracting each child TLV length from the declared SEQUENCE content length but never checks that the remainder is exactly zero. If children total more than declared, length goes negative and the loop exits silently returning e.g. 2 elements. Malformed DER with trailing/mismatched lengths is accepted as valid instead of throwing IOException, which can cause invalid ECDSA signatures to be accepted by asn1derToConcatenatedRS.

findings.title: integerToBytes silently mangles negative and oversized integers
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 151 integerToBytes converts DER INTEGER BigInteger to fixed-length bytes by truncating leading bytes if too long and zero-padding if too short. It does not reject negative values or values >= 2^(8*qLength). E.g. DER -1 (bytes 0xFF) becomes 32 bytes of 0x00..FF (255), and an oversized r/s is truncated to low bytes. Invalid out-of-range signature values are thus transformed into different in-range values instead of throwing IOException, hiding malformed signatures and enabling signature malleability.

findings.title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER lacks input length validation
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 103 concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature into r/s with len=signLength/2 and System.arraycopy without checking signature.length==signLength. A short or long input throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of declared IOException, and odd signLength silently drops a byte. Callers expecting IOException handling will get unexpected runtime exceptions.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns non-BouncyCastle provider
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 61 getBouncyCastleProvider contract states it returns the BouncyCastle security provider (FIPS or non-FIPS). Implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), typically SUN or SunJSSE, not BouncyCastle. Callers using the returned Provider for BC-specific algorithms will get wrong behavior or NoSuchAlgorithmException. Like WildFlyElytronProvider it should return null when BC is not used.

findings.title: AuthzClient.create poisons global CryptoIntegration singleton
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/AuthzClient.java line 95 create() calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). CryptoIntegration holds a static volatile singleton initialized only once and never re-evaluated for a different ClassLoader. If authz-client initializes first with a ClassLoader that only sees the fallback AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100), a later server init that could see Default/FIPS/Elytron (order 200) is ignored. In modular runtimes where visibility differs per loader this permanently locks in the weak provider and breaks server crypto.

findings.title: Test reuses P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only checks round-trip
findings.body: In authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java line 42 a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() (default P-256) is reused for ES256 (64 bytes), ES384 (96 bytes) and ES512 (132 bytes). Signing P-256 keys with SHA384/SHA512 still yields P-256 sized DER that is zero-padded to larger lengths, so the test passes without exercising real P-384/P-521 sizes. The test also only asserts asn1->concat->asn1 round-trip equality and never verifies with Signature.verify or known vectors, so truncation, leading-zero and negative-value bugs are not detected.
